user.title: Eberspächer EasyStart Web
user.description: Sign in with the account you use at myeberspaecher.com. This is an unofficial integration.

reauth_confirm.title: Sign in again
reauth_confirm.description: The saved login for {email} no longer works. Enter the current password.

error.no_devices: The account has no EasyStart Web devices
error.unknown: Unexpected error, see the Home Assistant log

abort.already_configured: This account is already set up

start_heating.name: Start heating
start_heating.description: Start the heater for a set time.

runtime.name: Run time
runtime.description: Minutes to run. Defaults to the Run time number.

mode.name: Mode
mode.description: Heating or ventilation. Defaults to the mode of the switch you call it on.

init.title: Options
init.description: What would you like to change?

polling.title: Polling
polling.description: How often to check the heater status while nothing is running. While it runs, and right after any start or stop from Home Assistant, it is checked regardless. With Off, starts made from the EasyStart app or website only show up after the next command from Home Assistant or a restart.

schedule.title: Schedule
schedule.description: Start the heater by itself so the car is ready at a set time. The colder it is, the earlier it starts (set the bands under Heating bands). Without a temperature sensor the heater's own last reading is used.

data_description.temperature_entity: Optional. A sensor with the outside temperature in °C.
data_description.notify_service: Optional. For example notify.mobile_app_your_phone. Gets a message when the heater starts, fails to start, or is not needed.

heating_bands.title: Heating bands
heating_bands.description: Above the first temperature the heater is not started. Each band below has its own run time, and its own start time worked out from the ready-by time.

ventilation.title: Summer ventilation
ventilation.description: When it is this warm or warmer, run the heater's ventilation instead of heating, so the car is cooler when you get in. Needs a heater that supports ventilation.

reminder.title: Idle reminder
reminder.description: A heater that sits unused for months should be run now and then so the fuel lines and pump stay in working order. When it has not run for this many days you get a message (through the notification service set under Schedule) and a notice under Repairs, repeated weekly until it runs.

data.car_check_enabled: Check weekly that the car answers

data_description.car_check_enabled: Every Sunday at 18:00 the car is asked for a temperature (this only reads, it never starts the heater). If it does not answer, you get a message and a notice under Repairs.

work.title: Leaving work
work.description: Also warm the car before you leave work, with the same heating bands. Needs the Schedule switch on. By default the temperature is the car's own: the heater is asked for a fresh reading and given 30 seconds to answer. You can choose a sensor for work instead. Nothing starts while your phone is at home.

data.work_enabled: Warm the car before leaving work

data_description.work_temperature_entity: Optional. A sensor or weather entity for the temperature at work. Leave empty to use the car's own reading.

learning.title: Learn departure times
learning.description: Learn when you usually get in the car and have it ready by then, for each weekday, instead of the fixed time. It needs a sensor that shows you got in (the iPhone Audio Output sensor shows CarPlay) and your phone's location. History Home Assistant already has is used right away. With fewer than 3 matching days the fixed time is used.

data.learn_state: State that means you got in

data_description.learn_entity: For example the iPhone's Audio Output sensor.
data_description.learn_tracker: The phone's device tracker or person.

hud.title: Sidebar panel
hud.description: Show the control panel (Optima) in the sidebar. It uses your Home Assistant login. On a phone, open it and use Share, then Add to Home Screen, to get a web app. The car sensors below are optional: choose them to show charge, fuel, range, odometer and 12 V battery in the panel.

error.runtime_too_long: The longest run time is longer than the time between midnight and the ready-by time
error.bands_order: The temperatures must go from warm to cold: No heating above, then Cold, then Very cold
error.vent_below_heating: Ventilation must start at a higher temperature than No heating above
error.learn_needs_signal: Choose both the departure sensor and the phone location
error.work_needs_tracker: Leaving work needs your phone's location, so it knows you are not at home. Choose it under Learn departure times first (learning itself can stay off).
error.learn_state_binary: A binary sensor is on or off: enter on (or off) as the state
error.notify_not_notify: Choose a notify service, for example notify.mobile_app_your_phone

cloud_unreachable.title: Eberspächer cloud unreachable
cloud_unreachable.description:
Home Assistant has not been able to reach myeberspaecher.com for several checks in a row. The last error was: {error}

If it keeps failing, check your internet and DNS settings, or whether the EasyStart Web service is down. The integration keeps trying and this notice goes away when it works again.

heater_idle.title: Car heater has not run for a while
heater_idle.description: The heater has not run for {days} days. Run it for about 10 minutes so the fuel lines and pump stay in working order. This notice goes away once it has run.

car_unreachable.title: Car unit not answering
car_unreachable.description:
{name} did not answer the weekly check: it was asked for a temperature and gave no answer within 3 minutes. The heater may not start from Home Assistant or the EasyStart app.

Check the car battery and that the EasyStart unit's SIM is active. This notice goes away after the next check that gets an answer, or once the heater runs.

runtime_range.message: Run time must be between {low} and {high} minutes for this heater
